examples.en: There's a stink coming from the shoe cabinet.
The stink from the drain made me open the window.
I sprayed air freshener to get rid of the stink.
The old cheese gave off a terrible stink.
I don't know where the stink is coming from.
The sweaty socks gave off a stink.

explain: 똥이나 썩은 것, 오래된 신발과 양말처럼 코를 찌르는 안 좋은 냄새예요. '고린내'는 비슷하지만 느낌이 조금 작은 말이에요. '냄새가 나다'보다 더 불쾌한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Something about this contract smells fishy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로는 괜찮아 보여도 뭔가 수상하고 떳떳하지 못한 느낌이 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is used when something seems suspicious or shady even though it looks fine on the surface.

explain_en: This is a nasty smell like feces, rotten things, or old shoes and socks. '고린내' is a similar word with a slightly smaller feel. It feels more unpleasant than just '냄새가 나다'.

examples.en: Don't say things like that.
There's no need to get mad over something like that.
I don't want to hear an excuse like that.
Why did you buy something like that?
Don't believe a rumor like that.
Stop thinking that kind of thought.

explain: '그런'과 비슷하지만 말하는 사람이 그것을 하찮게 보거나 못마땅해하는 느낌이 들어요. 그래서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 말로 '이딴', '저딴'이 있고, 가까운 사이에서 화나거나 가볍게 말할 때 나와요.
explain_en: Like 그런, but it sounds dismissive or disapproving, so don't use it with elders or people you just met. 이딴 and 저딴 are the same pattern, and you hear them among close friends when someone is annoyed or casual.

examples.ko: 까짓 시험 한 번 망쳤다고 포기하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't give up just because you blew one little test.
Ah, what the heck, let's give it a try.

examples.ko: 까짓 돈 몇 푼 때문에 싸우지 말아요.
examples.en: Don't fight over a measly bit of money.
Anyone makes a trifling mistake like that.

examples.ko: 까짓것 안 되면 다시 하면 돼요.
examples.en: So what if it doesn't work? You can just do it again.
So what if we get a little wet in the rain?

explain: 별것 아니라고 낮춰 말하거나 큰 결심을 가볍게 말할 때 써요. 뒤에는 '것, 거, 일, 돈'처럼 명사가 오고, '그까짓'은 더 강하게 말하는 형태예요. 친한 사이의 말투라서 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It is used to belittle something as trivial or to casually shrug off a big decision. A noun follows it, such as '것', '거', '일' or '돈', and '그까짓' is a stronger form. It is casual talk, so avoid it with seniors.

examples.ko: 가 보실 거예요? — 아무려면요, 꼭 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Are you going to go? — Of course, I'm definitely going.

examples.ko: 이 일 좀 도와줄 수 있어요? — 아무려면요, 맡겨 주세요.
examples.en: Can you help me with this? — Sure, leave it to me.

examples.ko: 내가 네 편이 아니면 누구 편이겠어요? 아무려면요.
examples.en: If I'm not on your side, whose side would I be on? Of course.

examples.ko: 그 약속을 잊었겠어요? 아무려면요, 벌써 적어 뒀어요.
examples.en: Would I forget that promise? Of course not, I already wrote it down.

examples.ko: 시험 잘 볼 수 있죠? — 아무려면요, 열심히 준비했어요.
examples.en: You can do well on the exam, right? — Sure, I prepared hard.

examples.ko: 다 먹었어요? — 아무려면요, 하나도 안 남겼어요.
examples.en: Did you finish it all? — Of course, I left nothing.

explain: 상대의 말에 '그렇고말고요' 하고 강하게 동의하거나 확인해 줄 때 써요. '아무렴'과 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 짝말이에요. 윗사람에게는 '그럼요', '물론이죠'가 더 무난해요.
explain_en: You use it to strongly agree with or confirm what the other person said, like 'you bet.' It is a variant of '아무렴' with the same meaning. To someone older or higher in status, '그럼요' or '물론이죠' is safer.

examples.en: You'll help, right? — Of course, don't worry.
Of course, you have to keep a promise.

examples.ko: 그 친구가 정직하냐고요? 아무렴요, 믿어도 돼요.
examples.en: Is that friend honest? Of course, you can trust him.

examples.ko: 이번에는 이길 수 있겠죠? — 아무렴요, 준비 많이 했어요.
examples.en: We can win this time, right? — Sure, we prepared a lot.
Of course, they're family, so naturally we help.
Health comes first? You bet, absolutely.

explain: 상대가 한 말이 맞다고 힘주어 맞장구칠 때 써요. 뒤에 '요'를 붙여 '아무렴요'라고도 하는데, 윗사람에게는 '그럼요'가 더 무난해요. 비슷한 말로 '그렇고말고요'가 있어요.
explain_en: You use it to back up what someone said with strong agreement. You can add 요 to say '아무렴요', but to a superior '그럼요' is safer. '그렇고말고요' is a similar expression.

examples.ko: 여분의 이불이 있으면 하나 빌려 주세요.
examples.en: If you have a spare blanket, please lend me one.

examples.ko: 회의 자료를 여분으로 몇 장 더 뽑았어요.
examples.en: I printed a few extra copies of the meeting materials.
I'm worried because I have no spare battery.
I put the extras in the storage room.
I took an extra pencil to the exam hall.
If there's any extra, I'll share it with my friend.

explain: 여분은 미리 더 챙겨 둔 것에 써요. 쓰고 남은 것은 '나머지'가 더 자연스러워요. '여분의 ○○'처럼 물건 앞에 자주 붙어요.
explain_en: 여분 is something you prepared in advance on top of what you need, like a spare. For what is left after using something, 나머지 sounds more natural. It often comes before a noun, as in 여분의 ○○.

examples.en: Someone shouted "Hear, hear!" during the meeting.
When the speech ended, people shouted "Hear, hear!"
A cry of "Hear, hear!" rang out through the auditorium.

examples.ko: 사극에서 신하들이 옳소 하고 외치는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There's a scene in the historical drama where the officials shout "Aye!"

examples.ko: 아버지는 제 말에 장난으로 "옳소!" 하고 박수를 치셨어요.
examples.en: My father playfully clapped and said "Hear, hear!" to what I said.

examples.ko: 토론장에서 "옳소!" 하는 소리와 야유가 동시에 나왔어요.
examples.en: In the debate hall, cries of "Hear, hear!" and jeers came out at the same time.

explain: 남의 말에 강하게 찬성할 때 크게 외치는 말이에요. 연설이나 토론, 집회 같은 곳에서 들을 수 있고, 일상 대화에서는 장난스럽게 쓰는 편이에요. 평소에는 '맞아요'나 '그래요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a word shouted out loud to strongly agree with someone's speech. You can hear it at speeches, debates and rallies, and in everyday talk it is used mostly playfully. Normally people say '맞아요' or '그래요'.

en: for this and that; for one thing or another

examples.ko: 요래조래 하다 보니 하루가 다 갔어요.
examples.en: What with one thing and another, the whole day was gone.
He kept making one excuse after another and put off the appointment.

examples.ko: 요래조래 따져 보면 이 가게가 제일 싸요.
examples.en: If you weigh it up every which way, this shop is the cheapest.

examples.ko: 아이가 요래조래 장난을 치며 놀고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is playing around, up to all sorts of mischief.

examples.ko: 요래조래 신경 쓸 일이 많아서 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: There are so many little things to worry about that I'm all in a whirl.

examples.ko: 이사 준비 때문에 요래조래 돈이 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: Preparing for the move cost a lot of money in one way or another.

explain: '이래저래'를 가볍고 귀엽게 말하는 구어예요. 친구나 가족끼리 편하게 말할 때 쓰고, 격식 있는 글에서는 '이래저래'나 '여러 가지로'를 써요. '하다 보니', '따져 보면'처럼 여러 일이 겹친 상황과 자주 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It is a light, cute colloquial version of '이래저래'. Use it with friends and family; in formal writing use '이래저래' or '여러 가지로'. It often appears with phrases like '하다 보니' or '따져 보면' when several things pile up.

examples.en: This is my first time with something like this, so I was flustered.

examples.ko: 요런 색깔 가방 혹시 다른 매장에도 있어요?
examples.en: Do other stores happen to have a bag in this color?
You definitely need an umbrella in weather like this.
Where did you buy such tasty bread?

examples.ko: 저는 요런 조용한 카페가 제일 좋아요.
examples.en: I like quiet cafes like this the best.

examples.ko: 요런 때는 그냥 웃어넘기는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: At times like this, it's best to just laugh it off.

explain: '이런'의 작은말로, 가까이 있는 작은 것을 가리키거나 귀엽고 가볍게 말할 때 써요. 친한 사이의 대화에서 많이 들리고, 격식 있는 글에서는 '이런'을 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '조런'이에요.
explain_en: It is the small-sounding form of '이런', used for something near and small or for a cute, light tone. It is common among close friends; in formal writing use '이런'. Its counterpart is '조런'.

examples.en: Hmm, I'll have to think about that.

examples.ko: 으음, 맛이 좀 이상한 것 같아요.
examples.en: Hmm, the taste seems a little strange.
Mm, that could be so.

examples.ko: 으음, 어디에 뒀는지 기억이 안 나요.
examples.en: Hmm, I can't remember where I put it.
Mm, I'm tired today and want to rest.
Hmm, a good idea just came to me!

explain: '으음'은 대답하기 전에 생각하거나 망설일 때 내는 소리예요. '음'보다 길게 끌어서 더 깊이 고민하는 느낌이 나요. 맞장구칠 때는 '응'이나 '네'를 써요.
explain_en: 으음 is a sound you make while thinking or hesitating before you answer. It is drawn out longer than 음 and sounds like deeper thought. To show you agree, you say 응 or 네.

en: for this and that; for one thing or another

examples.ko: 요즘 이래저래 바빠서 연락을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I've been busy with one thing and another lately, so I couldn't get in touch.

examples.ko: 이사하니까 이래저래 돈 쓸 일이 많아요.
examples.en: After moving, there are lots of things to spend money on.

examples.ko: 이래저래 걱정이 되어서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I'm worried about this and that, so I can't sleep.
This year had a lot of hard things, one way or another.
I tried this and that, but it was no use.

examples.ko: 이래저래 하다 보니 시간이 다 지나 버렸어요.
examples.en: Doing one thing and another, all the time slipped away.

explain: 이래저래는 여러 가지 이유나 상황이 겹쳤다는 느낌을 가볍게 말할 때 써요. '이럭저럭'은 '이럭저럭 지내요'처럼 그런대로 괜찮다는 느낌이라 달라요. 불평이나 변명을 부드럽게 할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 이래저래 lightly says that several reasons or situations piled up. 이럭저럭 differs: it means 'so-so, getting by', as in 이럭저럭 지내요. It often appears when you want to soften a complaint or an excuse.
